name: Inspect a running pod
objective: CKAD › Application Observability and Maintenance (15%). Goal: diagnose and fix failing workloads using kubectl logs, describe, and events — CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending (unschedulable), reading container stdout, and a failing readiness probe.

questions.title: Capture a line from container logs
questions.teach:
**`kubectl logs <pod>`** returns whatever the container wrote to **stdout/stderr** — run a pod that prints a line, then read it back. Store the captured value in a ConfigMap with **`kubectl create configmap <name> --from-literal=key=value`**.

**Gotcha:** `logs` only shows stdout/stderr — an app that writes to a file *inside* the container shows nothing.
questions.prompt:
Run a pod `logger` (image `busybox:1.36`) whose command prints the exact line `MARKER=ckad-obs-42` to stdout and then stays running (e.g. `echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600`). Read it back with `kubectl logs`, then create a ConfigMap `captured` in `ckad-observability` with key `token` set to that value `ckad-obs-42`.

Target: pod `logger` logged `MARKER=ckad-obs-42` AND ConfigMap `captured` has `token=ckad-obs-42`.
questions.hint: `kubectl run logger -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sh -c 'echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600'`, then `kubectl logs logger -n ckad-observability`, then `kubectl create configmap captured -n ckad-observability --from-literal=token=ckad-obs-42`.
questions.solution:
kubectl run logger -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sh -c 'echo MARKER=ckad-obs-42; sleep 3600'
kubectl logs logger -n ckad-observability   # MARKER=ckad-obs-42
kubectl create configmap captured -n ckad-observability --from-literal=token=ckad-obs-42

verification.description: logger printed the marker AND configmap 'captured' holds token=ckad-obs-42

questions.title: Debug a running pod with an ephemeral container
questions.teach:
`kubectl debug` attaches an **ephemeral container** to a *running* pod — a temporary debug container sharing the pod's namespaces, so you can troubleshoot an image that has no shell/tools without restarting it. `--target=<container>` shares that container's process namespace.

**Gotcha:** ephemeral containers can't be removed or restarted — they're for live debugging, not permanent sidecars.
questions.prompt:
Pod `blackbox` in `ckad-observability` is running but you can't `exec` into its container `app`. Use `kubectl debug` to add an **ephemeral debug container** (image `busybox:1.36`) targeting container `app`.

Target: pod `blackbox` has an ephemeral container using image `busybox:1.36`.
questions.hint: `kubectl debug -it blackbox -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --target=app -- sh` — the ephemeral container stays recorded on the pod even after you exit.
questions.solution:
kubectl debug -it blackbox -n ckad-observability --image=busybox:1.36 --target=app -- sh
# exit the shell; the ephemeral container remains on the pod
kubectl get pod blackbox -n ckad-observability -o jsonpath='{.spec.ephemeralContainers[*].image}'

verification.description: pod 'blackbox' has an ephemeral debug container (busybox:1.36)
